item.title: Meydan TV case in Azerbaijan: ‘Cancel trial and let us be punished under Ilham Aliyev’s decree’
item.description: As in previous hearings, the trial was again marked by tensions between the journalists and the panel of judges.

item.title: ‘Yerevan and Baku are on the same side in global geopolitical struggle’ – Armenian political scientist
item.description: According to Robert Ghevondyan, Armenia and Azerbaijan “accept US hegemony in a multipolar world, which is why there is greater confidence in the preservation of peace between them.”

item.title: More than 5,000 people killed in road accidents in Georgia over 10 years
item.description: The leading causes of road accidents are drink-driving and pedestrians crossing at unauthorised places.

item.title: Kaja Kallas says EU will demand Russian troops withdrawal from Georgian territories
item.description: It is one of the concessions Russia is expected to make during the ongoing negotiations with Ukraine.

item.title: Russia’s $90bn oil network: how Azerbaijani businessmen were exposed
item.description: The investigation shows that tankers linked to Azerbaijan became a key part of a sanctions-evasion network.

item.title: ‘Georgian government has effectively reversed its European course’, EU foreign affairs committee report says
item.description: The report, prepared by Rasa Juknevičienė, is set to be presented to the European Parliament’s Committee on Foreign Affairs on 25 February.

item.title: UK sanctions two Georgian TV channels over alleged spread of Russian disinformation
item.description: Sanctions against TV Imedi and POSTV include asset freezes, trust service bans and director disqualifications.

item.title: German envoy to Georgia addresses sanctions against Kulevi port, vetoed by Slovakia and Hungary
item.description: According to Peter Fischer, the Georgian authorities see Hungary as their “best friend” in the European Union, but that will not help them secure closer ties with the bloc.

item.title: Armenian parliament vice-speaker urges voters to ‘burn bridges with oligarchs’
item.description: According to Ruben Rubinyan, the upcoming elections should exclude both former presidents and the “two oligarchs” — Gagik Tsarukyan and Samvel Karapetyan — from political life.
